_comment: Design-review content for the two direction collages at /direction/a and /direction/b. Internal, noindex, never linked. Nothing here is site copy: every word a visitor would read on the real site is pulled from site.json and global.json. Delete this file and the /direction routes once a direction is chosen.

a.label: Direction A
a.name: The Reading Room
a.summary: Quiet, classical and text-led. The page behaves like a good literary journal: a fine serif does the talking, the portrait stands beside it like a frontispiece, and the terracotta appears only where a pencil would.

serif.note: Newsreader (Production Type, OFL). Drawn for long-form editorial reading, with a 6–72pt optical axis, so it turns fine and high-contrast at display size and sturdy at text size. Its italic carries the brand word.

sans.note: Hanken Grotesk (OFL). A calm, slightly warm grotesk that sits under the serif without competing. Figures are tabular by default, so prices align.

paletteNotes.paper: Warm uncoated stock, back toward the brief's Albescent White.
paletteNotes.band: A real second surface: 1.25:1 against the paper, twice today's step.
paletteNotes.dark: A deep ink-brown, the page's own shadow, so the close is in the same key as everything above it.

notes.hero: The brand line becomes the headline. The existing H1 wording stays the page's H1 for search, set as the lead beneath it. The portrait stands full height at the right edge as a frontispiece, graded ink-to-paper so it sits on the same stock as the type.
notes.type: Two families, six roles, one weight per role. Display, headings and leads are Newsreader 300, text is Hanken 400, emphasis is italic rather than bold. Labels are the only uppercase on the site.
notes.contents: The three services set as a contents page, not three boxes. Roman numerals in the italic, one rule above each entry.
notes.prices: Prices become a price list. The rate reads at body size with tabular figures, and the bundles sit on the line below. Same words, split at the existing middle dots.
notes.honours: Credentials set as a list of honours, with the qualification in the serif and no 12px uppercase.
notes.tracks: Before audio exists, one quiet track list instead of three disabled players. Each title keeps its pending tag and the note appears once. When audio arrives, each row becomes a player.
notes.essay: The name section becomes the essay moment: the lede at lead-plus size in the serif, then the manuscript photograph as a full-bleed band.
notes.controls: One filled button per screen. Links carry a clay underline that thickens on hover. Fields write on a rule, like lined paper.
notes.close: The close in ink-brown, with the wordmark's italic carried through.

b.label: Direction B
b.name: Printed Matter
b.summary: Tactile and image-led. The page behaves like an exhibition catalogue: photographs run wide in the shape they were shot, the type sits in their negative space, the grain is visible, and plum becomes a second key colour rather than a footer.

serif.note: Literata (TypeTogether, OFL). Designed as the reading face of Google Play Books, which suits a teacher of English. Sturdier and warmer than Newsreader, with a calligraphic italic, true small caps and old-style figures.

sans.note: Instrument Sans (OFL). A crisp contemporary grotesk with tabular figures, used small and sparingly.

paletteNotes.paper: A deeper, rosier stock, which lets the grain show.
paletteNotes.band: Used sparingly; plum carries the rhythm instead.
paletteNotes.dark: The brief's plum, promoted from footer to second key: the essay band, the close and the shadows of every photograph.

notes.hero: Chosen by the client: B, with the portrait from A. The photograph runs edge to edge in its own 3:2 shape and the brand line sits on the open wall to her left. The line is sized so it always ends inside that wall, from 1024px to 2560px. On the photograph the grade lifts the mid-tones and the italic is set in ink, which holds about 6:1 against the wall; the terracotta stays in the pencil line. On a phone the line sits on paper above the photograph.
notes.type: Literata and Instrument Sans. Labels use Literata's true small caps instead of tracked uppercase, and figures in prose are old-style, as in a book.
notes.contents: The services as large ruled rows, like chapter openings. The title leads, and the detail sits to the right.
notes.prices: A real price table: tier, lesson, rate and bundles in aligned columns on desktop, stacking on a phone.
notes.honours: Credentials in small caps with the awarding body beneath.
notes.tracks: The same quiet track list, set on the stone band so the voice section has its own room.
notes.essay: The lede becomes a pull-quote on a plum band, the brief's single dark mid-page moment, followed by the manuscript photograph.
notes.controls: A filled clay button, an underlined text link and lifted paper fields.
notes.close: The close in plum, matching the band above it, so the dark colour is a rhythm rather than an afterthought.
